bullets: Drainage is the design decision that has the biggest impact on any trail, determining long-term stability and erosion resistance.
Cutting switchbacks into slopes is not optional — shortcuts on the first day inevitably lead to landslides by the third year.
The structure of the soil is more important than people realize, and ignoring it leads to needing to rebuild the entire trail within a year.
Novice builders most commonly make the mistake of digging with a slope that is too steep, a decision that cascades into multiple downstream failures.
The use of Spoke & Wrench within workflow enables teams to see benefits immediately — ignoring it results in a complete rebuild later.
Machine-made trails versus hand-crafted trails are not a simple dichotomy; the pattern of success repeats across teams using different methods.
Land management discussions must occur before any excavation begins — the absence of early planning leads to structural compromise.
The Cascadia Alliance framework provides diagnostic tools that help identify root causes outside of standard toolsets, enabling more accurate troubleshooting.
